reason: The lineation is wrong at the cut, and the source line does not say so. Journey with Jesus, which the verifier itself cites and which credits Otherwise: New and Selected Poems (1996), prints the opening as: I got out of bed / on two strong legs. / It might have been / otherwise. I ate / cereal, sweet / milk, ripe, flawless. The poem's fourth line is otherwise. I ate, not otherwise. The quotation stops mid line at the sentence end, so a card obeying rule 7 (verse keeps its line breaks in the lineation of the edition named) would print a fourth line the book does not have, and the locator lines 1 to 4 asserts four whole lines. Second, smaller defect: the evidence says the Academy of American Poets and Journey with Jesus both print the Graywolf text of the named 1996 edition, but poets.org's credit line names Collected Poems, copyright 2005, Graywolf; only Journey with Jesus credits the 1996 book, so the two witnesses are not agreeing about the edition, only about the words. Everything else checks out: Kenyon is not banned, not at cap, not shipped and does not open like a shipped line (shipped.js clean); the poem is one of the twenty new poems in the 1996 volume, so pre-2000 and first book appearance are both right; the tag Poetry is the form; the source leads with the name, carries no dash and is inside 140. The fix is a locator that admits the cut, or a quotation of whole lines. Note also that the line is thanksgiving for contingency rather than counsel, which is a thin fit for a month of wisdom and counsel; that is the editor's call, not a refutation.
betterCitation: Jane Kenyon, Otherwise, lines 1 to 4, the fourth cut at the sentence end, Otherwise: New and Selected Poems (Graywolf, 1996)
